title: Accompanying singers and early recording methods
summary: Scott does not remember the singers and describes one-mike acoustic recording.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And Edna Hicks?
Uh-huh.
Rose Henderson? Now, Alberta, do you remember recording with Alberta?
She was at Lafayette, mostly, but I don't remember recording with her.
You don't remember recording with her.
No.
Viola McCoy?
You see, when I made those records, we didn't have singers. We didn't have singers, these were just musical.
But you were accompanying these singers.
Maybe there were in a different room or something. I didn't see them.
Really?
Because in those days, they made records funny. They do it different now. Each section in the band has a mike in front of it. But then you only had one mike.
And then they didn't even have a mike, they had a horn. George Williams.
Who?
George Williams.
Yeah, old George.
He's from Columbia, June 27, 1924.
Yeah.
You made a couple of things (inaudible). And who was he?
Hm?
Who was George Williams? Was he a comedian or --
He was a showman, but he wasn't no regular singer. And I can't -- those singers are so far back.
Well, of course, yeah.
And so much has happened in between, that unless you can put it right down to the very minute it's done
and recorded, it skips your mind. You have to delve in your mind and think way back then.
